Pense em um baralho bem embaralhado. Se.en:
Think of a well-shuffled deck. If 70% of the cards are `A` and 30% are `a`, drawing two cards to form each animal makes some combinations more likely than others. Two `A` cards are more likely than two `a` cards because the deck contains more `A` cards.

With `p = 0,7` and `q = 0,3`, the probability of `AA` is `0,7 x 0,7`; the probability of `Aa` is `0,7 x 0,3` in one order plus `0,3 x 0,7` in the reverse order; and the probability of `aa` is `0,3 x 0,3`. These combinations give `p^2`, `2pq` and `q^2`.

The analogy has limits. A horse herd is not a perfect deck: it may be small, include relatives, use selected breeding animals or have sex-specific structure. Hardy–Weinberg should therefore provide a comparison expectation, not a dogma about the real herd.
Pense em um baralho bem embaralhado. Se.es:
Piensa en una baraja bien mezclada. Si el 70% de las cartas son `A` y el 30% son `a`, al sacar dos cartas para formar cada animal algunas combinaciones resultan más probables que otras. Dos cartas `A` son más probables que dos `a` porque hay más cartas `A`.

Con `p = 0,7` y `q = 0,3`, la probabilidad de `AA` es `0,7 x 0,7`; la de `Aa` es `0,7 x 0,3` en un orden más `0,3 x 0,7` en el orden inverso; y la de `aa` es `0,3 x 0,3`. Estas combinaciones producen `p^2`, `2pq` y `q^2`.

La analogía tiene límites. Un plantel de caballos no es una baraja perfecta: puede ser pequeño, incluir parientes, utilizar reproductores seleccionados o tener estructura por sexo. Por eso, Hardy–Weinberg debe proporcionar una expectativa de comparación, no un dogma sobre el plantel real.

Considere `p = 0,7` e `q = 0,3`. A frequ.en:
Consider `p = 0,7` and `q = 0,3`. The expected frequency of `AA` is `0,49`, that of `Aa` is `0,42`, and that of `aa` is `0,09`. In 100 animals, this corresponds to 49 `AA`, 42 `Aa` and 9 `aa`.

You have reached the checkpoint if you can explain the difference between observed and expected. Observed means the actual count in the table. Expected means the number predicted by the formula from `p` and `q`. If the observed counts are 52 `AA`, 38 `Aa` and 10 `aa`, they are close to the expectation, but do not equal it.

Considere oito cavalos em um exemplo did.en:
Consider eight horses in a didactic example of height. Each animal has three loci, and each locus can contribute 0, 1 or 2 units. First we will ignore the environment to see only the polygenic sum.

| Animal | `L1` | `L2` | `L3` | `G = L1 + L2 + L3` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A | 0 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| B | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
| C | 1 | 1 | 1 | 3 |
| D | 1 | 1 | 2 | 4 |
| E | 2 | 1 | 1 | 4 |
| F | 2 | 2 | 1 | 5 |
| G | 2 | 2 | 2 | 6 |
| H | 0 | 2 | 0 | 2 |

Animal A has low sum, `G = 1`. The animal G has high sum, `G = 6`. Among them are intermediate values: 2, 3, 4 and 5. This is the first important point. Even with only three loci, the trait no longer seems to be a simple division into two classes.

The average of `G` in this group is:

`media = (1 + 3 + 3 + 4 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 2) / 8 = 28 / 8 = 3,5`

The average value of the group is 3,5 units. Animals A and H are below average; D and E are slightly above; G is well above. The average helps to locate the center, but the table shows that there is variation. If we only looked at the average, we would lose the information that there are animals from 1 to 6 units.

Now add a didactic environmental deviation:

| Animal | `G` | `E` | `P = G + E` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| B | 3 | 0 | 3 |
| C | 3 | -1 | 2 |
| D | 4 | 1 | 5 |
| E | 4 | 0 | 4 |
| F | 5 | -1 | 4 |
| G | 6 | 0 | 6 |
| H | 2 | 1 | 3 |

The environment does not create polygenic inheritance, but changes the observed value. C and B have the same `G = 3`, but end up with different phenotypes because their environmental deviations are different. D and F have different genotypic values, but are close to the observed phenotype. This is the link with M6: the phenotype is still a sum of genotype and environment. The novelty of M7 is that the didactic genotype can be seen as a sum of many small effects.
Considere oito cavalos em um exemplo did.es:
Considere ocho caballos en un ejemplo didáctico de altura. Cada animal tiene tres loci, y cada locus puede aportar 0, 1 o 2 unidades. Primero ignoraremos el ambiente para ver sólo la suma poligénica.

| Animal | `L1` | `L2` | `L3` | `G = L1 + L2 + L3` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A | 0 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| B | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
| C | 1 | 1 | 1 | 3 |
| D | 1 | 1 | 2 | 4 |
| E | 2 | 1 | 1 | 4 |
| F | 2 | 2 | 1 | 5 |
| G | 2 | 2 | 2 | 6 |
| H | 0 | 2 | 0 | 2 |

Animal A tiene baja suma, `G = 1`. El animal G tiene suma alta, `G = 6`. Entre ellos hay valores intermedios: 2, 3, 4 y 5. Este es el primer punto importante. Incluso con sólo tres loci, la característica ya no parece ser una simple división en dos clases.

El promedio de `G` en este grupo es:

`media = (1 + 3 + 3 + 4 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 2) / 8 = 28 / 8 = 3,5`

El valor promedio del grupo es 3,5 unidades. Los animales A y H están por debajo de la media; D y E están ligeramente por encima; G está bien por encima. El promedio ayuda a localizar el centro, pero la tabla muestra que hay variación. Si sólo miramos el promedio, perderíamos la información de que hay animales de 1 a 6 unidades.

Ahora agregue una desviación ambiental didáctica:

| Animal | `G` | `E` | `P = G + E` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| B | 3 | 0 | 3 |
| C | 3 | -1 | 2 |
| D | 4 | 1 | 5 |
| E | 4 | 0 | 4 |
| F | 5 | -1 | 4 |
| G | 6 | 0 | 6 |
| H | 2 | 1 | 3 |

El ambiente no crea la herencia poligénica, sino que cambia el valor observado. C y B tienen el mismo `G = 3`, pero terminan con diferentes fenotipos porque sus desviaciones ambientales son diferentes. D y F tienen diferentes valores genotípicos, pero están cerca del fenotipo observado. Este es el enlace con M6: el fenotipo sigue siendo una suma de genotipo y medio ambiente. La novedad de M7 es que el genotipo didáctico se puede ver como una suma de muchos efectos pequeños.

A analogia é DNA como mapa e pista. Às v.en:
Think of DNA as both a map and a set of clues. Sometimes the map answers "who is related to whom?" That is the question addressed by matrix `G`. Sometimes it highlights a region with a strong signal. That is the question addressed by GWAS. Sometimes we use the whole map to predict the likely genetic merit of a young animal before many of its offspring have been evaluated. That is the question addressed by genomic prediction.

Matrix `G` maps molecular relatedness. Two animals may have similar pedigrees yet share more or fewer markers than expected. Matrix `G` summarizes the similarity observed across these markers.

GWAS searches for local clues. It examines each SNP and asks whether the marker is associated with a phenotypic difference. Results are often displayed in a Manhattan plot: each point is a marker, and higher peaks indicate stronger statistical associations. A peak does not automatically establish a causal gene; it identifies a signal worth investigating.

Genomic prediction uses markers collectively to predict. Instead of focusing on one peak, it combines many small signals. GBLUP uses genomic relationships, represented by matrix `G`, within a mixed-model framework. The practical question is whether the predictions work for animals that were not used to train the model.
A analogia é DNA como mapa e pista. Às v.es:
Imagina el ADN como un mapa y un conjunto de pistas. A veces el mapa responde "¿quién está emparentado con quién?" Esa es la pregunta que aborda la matriz `G`. A veces destaca una región con una señal fuerte. Esa es la pregunta que aborda GWAS. A veces utilizamos el mapa completo para predecir el mérito genético probable de un animal joven antes de evaluar a muchos de sus descendientes. Esa es la pregunta que aborda la predicción genómica.

La matriz `G` representa el parentesco molecular. Dos animales pueden tener pedigríes similares y, aun así, compartir más o menos marcadores de lo esperado. La matriz `G` resume la semejanza observada en esos marcadores.

GWAS busca pistas locales. Examina cada SNP y pregunta si el marcador está asociado con una diferencia fenotípica. Los resultados suelen representarse en un gráfico de Manhattan: cada punto es un marcador y los picos más altos indican asociaciones estadísticas más fuertes. Un pico no demuestra automáticamente que un gen sea causal; identifica una señal que merece investigación.

La predicción genómica utiliza los marcadores en conjunto para predecir. En lugar de centrarse en un pico, combina muchas señales pequeñas. GBLUP utiliza el parentesco genómico, representado por la matriz `G`, dentro de un modelo mixto. La pregunta práctica es si las predicciones funcionan en animales que no se utilizaron para entrenar el modelo.

A analogia é ajustar uma régua torta ant.en:
The analogy is adjusting a miscalibrated ruler before measuring animals. If a ruler starts 2 cm above zero, every measurement is too large. You cannot conclude that an animal measured with that ruler is larger without correcting the ruler’s error. First adjust the ruler; then compare the animals.

Farm conditions can act like a miscalibrated ruler. Sex can do the same. If males are heavier on average than females, comparing a male from a favorable farm with a female from an unfavorable farm confounds animal, sex and environment. The model asks how much of the measurement belongs to the known group and how much remains attributable to the animal and error.

A fixed effect is like a ruler we want to adjust directly. If the course compares exactly two farms and two sexes, we can estimate the mean differences between these groups and adjust the measurements. A random effect is different: its levels are viewed as a sample from a larger population of effects. The residual is what remains after the model has accounted for the terms specified in its formula.
A analogia é ajustar uma régua torta ant.es:
La analogía consiste en ajustar una regla mal calibrada antes de medir a los animales. Si una regla empieza 2 cm por encima del cero, todas sus mediciones resultan mayores. No se puede concluir que un animal medido con esa regla es más grande sin corregir el error. Primero ajustamos la regla; después comparamos los animales.

Las condiciones de la granja pueden actuar como una regla mal calibrada. El sexo también. Si los machos son, en promedio, más pesados que las hembras, comparar un macho de una granja favorable con una hembra de una granja desfavorable confunde animal, sexo y ambiente. El modelo pregunta cuánto de la medición corresponde al grupo conocido y cuánto queda atribuible al animal y al error.

Un efecto fijo es como una regla que queremos ajustar directamente. Si el curso compara exactamente dos granjas y dos sexos, podemos estimar las diferencias medias entre esos grupos y ajustar las mediciones. Un efecto aleatorio es distinto: sus niveles se consideran una muestra de una población mayor de efectos. El residuo es lo que queda después de considerar los términos especificados en la fórmula del modelo.

A analogia é um código de barras genétic.en:
Think of a genetic barcode. A product barcode does not describe the entire product, but helps identify patterns. A SNP panel works similarly: it does not read the whole genome in full detail, but observes many specific positions where animals may differ.

A SNP involves variation at a DNA position. Some animals may carry allele `A` and others allele `B`. Horses are diploid, so each carries two copies at that position, one from each parent. When counting allele `B`, the genotype can therefore be coded as `0`, `1` or `2`.

Code `0` means no copies of the counted allele; `1` means one copy; and `2` means two. Thus, `0` can represent `AA`, `1` can represent `AB`, and `2` can represent `BB` when `B` is counted. The allele letters depend on the marker, but the counting logic stays the same.
A analogia é um código de barras genétic.es:
Piensa en un código de barras genético. El código de barras de un producto no lo describe por completo, pero ayuda a identificar patrones. Un panel de SNP funciona de manera similar: no lee todo el genoma en detalle, sino muchas posiciones concretas en las que pueden diferir los animales.

Un SNP implica variación en una posición del ADN. Algunos animales pueden llevar el alelo `A` y otros el alelo `B`. Los caballos son diploides, por lo que cada uno lleva dos copias en esa posición, una de cada progenitor. Al contar el alelo `B`, el genotipo puede codificarse como `0`, `1` o `2`.

El código `0` significa ninguna copia del alelo contado; `1` significa una copia; y `2` significa dos. Así, `0` puede representar `AA`, `1` puede representar `AB` y `2` puede representar `BB` cuando se cuenta `B`. Las letras dependen del marcador, pero la lógica del recuento se mantiene.

A fórmula central da unidade é:\n\n`DEP.en:
The central formula of the unit is:

`DEP = EBV / 2`

Where:

- `DEP` is the expected difference in progeny;
- `EBV` is the estimated breeding value of the animal;
- both must be in the same unit of the trait;
- dividing by 2 represents the average expectation of transmission to offspring.

If a stallion has `EBV = 20` points for a didactic performance index, then:

`DEP = 20 / 2 = 10`

Biologically, this means that, on average, the progeny of this stallion is expected to have 10 more points than the basis of comparison, in the conditions and assumptions of the evaluation. It does not mean that all offspring will be 10 upper points. DEP is average expectation, not individual promise.

We will also use a simple phenotypic correction:

`fenotipo_corrigido = fenotipo_observado - efeito_ambiente`

Here, `efeito_ambiente` is a didactic adjustment of a known effect. If an animal had an environment advantage of `+8` points, we removed this advantage to compare more fairly. This is not yet a linear model, mixed model or BLUP. In M16, this type of adjustment will be formalized with models; in M17, it will be linked to genetic evaluation with BLUP.

A fórmula central é:\n\n`R = h2 * S`\n\n.en:
The central formula is:

`R = h2 * S`

Where:

- `R` is the expected response to selection, in the unit of the trait per generation;
- `h2` is the heritability in the restricted sense, without unity, between 0 and 1 in the exercise;
- `S` is the selection differential, in the unit of the trait.

If `h2 = 0,30` and `S = 20` points, then:

`R = 0,30 * 20 = 6`

Biologically, the next generation is expected 6 points above the original average, not 20 points. The 20 points represent the average phenotypic superiority of the selected parents. The expected response is lower because only part of this superiority is attributed to additive genetic variation.

To consider time, we used:

`ganho_por_ano = R / L`

Where `L` is the generation interval in years. If `R = 6` points per generation and `L = 8` years:

`ganho_por_ano = 6 / 8 = 0,75`

This means that the expected average gain, distributed by time, is 0,75 point per year. Biological gain happens per generation, but planning needs to see time.

A fórmula central é:\n\n`VP = VA + VD +.en:
The central formula is:

`VP = VA + VD + VI + VE`

Where:

- `VP` is the total phenotypic variance;
- `VA` is the additive genetic variance;
- `VD` is the dominance variance;
- `VI` is the variance of epistatic interaction;
- `VE` is the environmental variance.

All terms are on the same variance scale. If the example uses points of variance, all components are also points of variation. If the trait was measured in g/day, a real variance would be in `(g/dia)^2`.

This sum is a simple partition within the model adopted in the exercise. It assumes that the components are being treated separately and does not include other possible sources or relationships, such as covariances between components or genotype-environment interaction. Therefore, the formula is a class organization tool, not a universal law for any data design.

We will also use the additive fraction:

`h2 = VA / VP`

In this unit, `h2` will be used only as the fraction of the phenotypic variance explained by `VA`, because the task of M8 asks to interpret this fraction. The most complete interpretation of heritability is for M9. Here, the use is operational: calculate the additive fraction to understand why `VA` is central to selection.

If `VA = 40` and `VP = 100`, then:

`h2 = 40 / 100 = 0,40`

Biologically, this means that 40% of the phenotypic variation of the example is in the additive part of the model. It does not mean that 40% of the phenotype of an individual animal is "genetic". The account speaks of the variation between animals of a population, not of the composition of an isolated animal.

A fórmula didática do cálculo manual des.en:
The didactic formula of the manual calculation of this unit is:

`EBV_didatico = h2 * y`

Where:

- `y` is the phenotypic deviation of the animal in relation to the average of the comparable group;
- `h2` is the heritability in the restricted sense, in scale from `0` to `1`;
- `EBV_didatico` is a simple shrunk prediction in the same unit of `y`.

If the young stallion had `y = 20` points and the trait has `h2 = 0,30`, then:

`EBV_didatico = 0,30 * 20 = 6`

Biologically, the number `6` says: the gross difference of `20` points should not be read as `20` points of additive genetic merit. With moderate heritability, part of the observed difference can come from environment and Residual. The value collected is lower because the model does not transfer all the observation to the breeding value.

This calculation is not BLUP complete. The name `EBV_didatico` is only a pedagogical label for a simple shrink prediction. The complete BLUP adjusts fixed effects, uses kinship relationships, combines information from several animals and depends on variance components. The miniature serves for the student to see the principle before entering the matrix.

The factor `lambda` helps to understand the shrinkage force. In the simplified case of this class, assuming that the phenotypic variation was separated into additive genetic and residual part, we can write:

`lambda = (1 - h2) / h2`

If `h2 = 0,30`, then:

`lambda = 0,70 / 0,30 = 2,33`

Higher value of `lambda` indicates that the Residual weighs more than the additive genetic variation. In this case, the model should rely less on raw individual deviation and shrink more prediction. If `h2` increases, `lambda` decreases, and the observed deviation receives more genetic weight.
A fórmula didática do cálculo manual des.es:
La fórmula didáctica del cálculo manual de esta unidad es:

`EBV_didatico = h2 * y`

Donde:

- `y` es la desviación fenotípica del animal en relación con el promedio del grupo comparable;
- `h2` es la heredabilidad en el sentido restringido, en escala de `0` a `1`;
- `EBV_didatico` es una simple predicción con contracción en la misma unidad de `y`.

Si el joven semental tenía `y = 20` puntos y la característica tiene `h2 = 0,30`, entonces:

`EBV_didatico = 0,30 * 20 = 6`

Biológicamente, el número `6` dice: la diferencia bruta de `20` puntos no debe ser leído como `20` puntos de mérito genético aditivo. Con heredabilidad moderada, parte de la diferencia observada puede provenir del medio ambiente y el residuo. El valor recogido es menor porque el modelo no transfiere toda la observación al valor genético.

Este cálculo no es BLUP completo. El nombre `EBV_didatico` es sólo una etiqueta pedagógica para una simple predicción con contracción. El completo BLUP ajusta los efectos fijos, utiliza las relaciones de parentesco, combina información de varios animales y depende de componentes de varianza. La miniatura sirve para que el estudiante vea el principio antes de entrar en la matriz.

El factor `lambda` ayuda a entender la fuerza de contracción. En el caso simplificado de esta clase, asumiendo que la variación fenotípica se separó en parte genética y residual aditiva, podemos escribir:

`lambda = (1 - h2) / h2`

Si. `h2 = 0,30`, entonces:

`lambda = 0,70 / 0,30 = 2,33`

El valor más alto de `lambda` indica que el residuo pesa más que la variación genética aditiva. En este caso, el modelo debe depender menos de la desviación individual cruda y reducir más predicción. Si. `h2` aumentos, `lambda` disminuye, y la desviación observada recibe más peso genético.

A fórmula geral de correlação é:\n\n`r =.en:
The general correlation formula is:

`r = covxy / sqrt(vx * vy)`

Where:

- `r` is the correlation between the traits `x` and `y`;
- `covxy` is the covariance between `x` and `y`;
- `vx` is the variance of `x`;
- `vy` is the variance of `y`;
- `sqrt(vx * vy)` standardizes covariance for scale from -1 to 1.

If `x` is weight and `y` is fat thickness, the formula measures how much the weight and fat deviations go together, adjusting for the size of the variation of each trait.

For different types of correlation, the logic is the same, but the components change:

`rP = covPxy / sqrt(VPx * VPy)`

`rA = covAxy / sqrt(VAx * VAy)`

`rE = covExy / sqrt(VEx * VEy)`

`rP` uses covariance and phenotypic variances. `rA` uses covariance and additive genetic variances. `rE` uses covariance and environmental variances. The error we want to avoid is to look `rP` and automatically conclude that the association is genetic.
A fórmula geral de correlação é:\n\n`r =.es:
La fórmula de correlación general es:

`r = covxy / sqrt(vx * vy)`

Donde:

- `r` es la correlación entre las características `x` y `y`;
- `covxy` es la covarianza entre `x` y `y`;
- `vx` es la diferencia de `x`;
- `vy` es la diferencia de `y`;
- `sqrt(vx * vy)` estandariza la covarianza para escala de -1 a 1.

Si `x` es peso y `y` es grosor de grasa, la fórmula mide cuánto el peso y las desviaciones de grasa van juntas, ajustando para el tamaño de la variación de cada característica.

Para diferentes tipos de correlación, la lógica es la misma, pero los componentes cambian:

`rP = covPxy / sqrt(VPx * VPy)`

`rA = covAxy / sqrt(VAx * VAy)`

`rE = covExy / sqrt(VEx * VEy)`

`rP` utiliza la covarianza y las diferencias fenotípicas. `rA` usa covarianza y variabilidades genéticas aditivas. `rE` utiliza covariance y varias ambientales. El error que queremos evitar es mirar `rP` y concluir automáticamente que la asociación es genética.

A herdabilidade não é uma propriedade fi.en: Heritability is not a fixed property of the trait

A segregação explica por que um animal n.en:
The segregation explains why an animal does not receive all the alleles of the father or all allele of the mother. It receives a copy in each locus of each parent. When the parent is `Aa`, it can transmit `A` or `a`.

What is observed in the animal is the phenotype. What he carries in the pair of alleles is the genotype. The class is correct when these two layers are not confused.

Error that this unit must avoid: writing "the animal is `A`". Animal is not allele. Animal has genotype, for example `Aa`, and may present a phenotype, for instance present trait.
A segregação explica por que um animal n.es:
La segregación explica por qué un animal no recibe todos los alelos del padre o alelo de la madre. Recibe una copia en cada locus de cada padre. Cuando el padre es `Aa`, puede transmitir `A` o `a`.

Lo que se observa en el animal es el fenotipo. Lo que lleva en el par de alelos es el genotipo. La clase es correcta cuando estas dos capas no se confunden.

Error que esta unidad debe evitar: escribir "el animal es `A`". El animal no es alelo. El animal tiene genotipo, por ejemplo `Aa`, y puede presentar un fenotipo, como la característica presente.

|---|---|---|
| Was there heterosis? | `F1` against parental mean | Yes, `F1 = 230` against parental mean `215` |
